newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA BEAT FRANCE IN DOUBLES FOR 3-0 LEAD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA BEAT FRANCE IN DOUBLES FOR 3-0 LEAD.

text.p: Australians Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde, the world's leading tennis duo, on Saturday ended France's brief grip on the Davis Cup by winning the decisive doubles match in their World Group first round tie.
Woodbridge and Woodforde, winners of 42 career titles together, defeated the French pair of Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux 7-6 (8-6) 6-4 6-3, to hand Australia an unbeatable 3-0 lead in the tie.
The match started as a tense affair, with Forget and Raoux battling to stave off defeat for France after losses in the opening two singles matches in Sydney on Friday.
However, the Australians, known as the "Woodies", gradually began to pull ahead after winning a close first set tie-breaker.

The experience of the Australians, the reigning Wimbledon, U.S., Australian and Olympic doubles champions, proved insurmountable for the Frenchmen, whose service games began to deteriorate as the match wore on.
Both pairs started nervously and concentrated on playing an error-free game, rather than taking an aggressive approach.
Raoux cracked first when he lost a point on his serve in the first set tie-breaker, with Forget then dropping his serve in the first game of the second set.
Australia's win marked a triumphant return from the Davis Cup wilderness for the 26-time winner, which two years ago was relegated to the event's regional competition.

Australia's victory in the tie was set on Friday, when Patrick Rafter fought back after losing the first two sets to beat French number one Cedric Pioline. Woodforde then downed Arnaud Boetsch in straight sets.

France won the Davis Cup by beating Sweden 3-2 in the final in dramatic circumstances nine weeks ago, fighting back from 0-2 down. The French were, however, unable to repeat their heroic performance in sweltering heat on the grass courts of Sydney's White City.
